                 MAXIMUM PRICES FOR BREAD—LAE
  MEKERE MORAUTA, Price Controller, by virtue of the powers
conferred by the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as
 amended to date, and all other powers me enabling, do hereby make
the following Order:—
                      PRICES ORDER No. 127
1. CITATION.
  This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 127.
2. COMMENCEMENT.
  This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication of
this Order in the Gazette.
3. REVOCATION.
  Prices Order No. 93 is hereby revoked.
4. DEFINITIONS.
  In this Order—
    "bread" means a product obtained by making a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with
      or without other ingredients;
    "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery
      to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was
      so enclosed when sold;
    "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per centurn
      by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the water-free
substance;


No. 21-27th March, 1975                                         2

Papua New Guinea Gazette


                                       Maximum Prices for Bread—Lae—
continued


        "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or


             milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;


        "wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery to


             the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
waxed or grease-proof paper, cellulose film, polythene or


             other similar wrapping and that such bread was so
enclosed when sold;


        "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in this


             Order.


5. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.


     Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be measured


when the bread is cold.


6. MAXIMUM PRICE.


     I fix and declare the maximum price at which bread included in
a category described in the first column of

the Schedule to this Order may be sold by wholesale and retail in
the City of Lae to be the price specified in the


second column of that Schedule opposite to the description of that
category.


7. DISPLAY OF PRICES.


     A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the City of Lae, shall display in each of their


places of business, in prominent positions and in large clear and
legible figures, the types of bread loaves covered


by this Order and the prices at which such loaves may be bought.

                           MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICES FOR BREAD—PORT

    MEKERE MORAUTA, Price Controller, by virtue of the powers
conferred by the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as


   amended to date, and all other powers me enabling, do hereby make
the following Order:—


                                                   PRICES ORDER No.
128


1. CITATION.


      This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 128.


2. COMMENCEMENT.


     This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazelle.


3. REVOCATION.


      Prices Order No. 93 is hereby revoked.


4. DEFINITIONS.

In this Order—


        "bread" means a product obtained by baking a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with or

             without other ingredients;


Papua New Guinea Gazette

                                      Maximum Retail Prices for Bread—

         "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread
that such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery


                to the place at which the bread is sold by retail,
in aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was so


                enclosed when sold;


         "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and
which contains no less than four parts per centuni


                by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the
water-free substance;


         "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or


                milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;

"starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread" means
bread which is made into loaves and which con-


                tains not less than two and seven-tenths parts per
centum by weight of nitrogen calculated on the water-


                free substance;


         "wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery to


                the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
waxed or grease-proof paper, cellulose film, polythene


                or other similar wrapping and that such bread was so
enclosed when sold;


         "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in this


                Order.


5. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.


     Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be measured


when the bread is cold,


6. MAXIMUM PRICE.


      I fix and declare the maximum price at which bread included in
a category described in the first column of


the Schedule to this Order may be sold by retail in the City of Port
Moresby to be the price specified in the second

column of that Schedule opposite to the description of that
category.


7. DISPLAY OF PRICES.


      A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the City of Port Moresby, shall display in each


of their places of business, in prominent positions and in large
clear and legible figures, the types of bread loaves


covered by this Order and the prices at which such loaves may be
bought.

                                 Electoral Act 1963-1971

NOMINATION OF CANDIDATES AND LOCATION OF POLLING PLACES FOR ELECTION
OF
                      MEMBER TO THE HOUSE OF ASSEMBLY
THE following persons have been duly nominated as candidates for the
By-election of Poroma-Kutubu Open
   Electorate in the House of Assembly for Papua New Guinea:—
     Koni Iorei
     Proenaike Om
     Sage Kuburu
     Tombol Ungunaibe
   A Poll will accordingly be taken for the Electorate on Saturday
the 12th April, 1975, in accordance with the
laws of Papua New Guinea for the regulation of Elections in the
House of Assembly.
   The Poll for the said Election will open at eight o'clock in the
morning on Saturday, 12th April, 1975,
and that the polling period will not close until all electors
desiring to vote have voted in the polling booth at
six o'clock on the day of the polling period. It is a two week poll
for the said Election and that all Electors are
advised that no further voting will take place after six o'clock on
26th March, 1975.

POSITION OF DISTRICT COMMISSIONER

Applications are invited from suitably qualified persons both from
inside and outside the
Public Service of Papua New Guinea for two positions of District
Commissioner.

Appointment will be initially on a temporary basis with salary at
either the Class 11
($7,135) or Class 10 ($6,445-$6,675) salary levels, depending upon
experience and ability.
Successful applicants will be required to undergo a period of on-
the-job training before
advancement to District Commissioner, a level 1 appointment with an

annual salary of
$7,365.

Appointment as District Commissioner will be for three years and
will he subject to review
at the end of that term. An officer whose term of appointment is not
renewed will be placed
in a position with a salary classification not less than he held
before being selected for
training. For those persons engaged from outside the Public Service
the question of
continued employment will be subject to negotiation towards the end
of the period of
appointment.

Experience within the Department is oot essential. The Public
Service is seeking experierical
men with a high level of administrative and executive potential.
Applicants should have the
Public Service Higher Certificate or Form 6 or such other
educational qualifications as may
be acceptable to the Public Service Board.

Appointees after a short period of training will be appointed to a
District and will be
responsible to the Chief Minister for the co-ordination of
government policies and activities
in the district and the social, political and economic advancement
of the district.

                             MAXIMUM PRICES FOR BREAD—PORT MORESBY


il MEKERE MORAUTA, Price Controller, by virtue of the powers
conferred by the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as

   amended to date, and all other powers me enabling, do hereby make
the following Order:—


                                             PRICES ORDER No. 134


 1. CITATION.

This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 134.


 2. COMMENCEMENT.


     This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazette.


 3. REVOCATION.


     Prices Order No. 128 is hereby revoked.


 4. DEFINITIONS.


     In this Order—


       "bread" means a product obtained by baking a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with or

           without other ingredients;


       "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or

           milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;


       "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per cent=

           by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the water-
free substance;


       "starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread" means
bread which is made into loaves and which con-

           tains not less than two and seven-tenths part per centum
by weight of nitrogen calculated on the water-

           free substance;


       "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in this

           Order.

"wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery to the

           place at which the bread is sold by retail, in waxed or
grease-proof paper, cellulose film, polythene or

           other similar wrapping and that such bread was so
enclosed when sold;


       "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread
that such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery

           to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was


           so enclosed when sold;


 5. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.


     Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be measured

when the bread is cold.


6. MAXIMUM PRICE.


     I fix and declare the maximum price at which bread included in
a category described in the first column of

the Schedule to this Order may be sold by retail in the City of Port
Moresby to be the price specified in the second

column of that Schedule opposite to the description of that
category.


 7. DISPLAY OF PRICES.


     A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the City of Port Moresby, shall display in each

of their places of business, in prominent positions and in large
clear and legible figures, the types of bread loaves

covered by this Order and the prices at which such loaves may be

bought.

                           DESCRIPTION OF CURRENCY

AS required under Section 51(2) of the Central Banking Act 1973, the
denominations and other character-
  istics of Papua New Guinea legal tender currency issued by the
Bank of Papua New Guinea are as follows:—
1. BANKNOTES
     2 Kina — 140 MM x 70 MM
     5 Kina — 145 MM x 72.5 MM
    10 Kina — 150 MM x 75 MM
   The paper used is mould made panel banknote paper with a
substance of 83 grams per square metre into which
is incorporated a formal watermark of the Bank of Papua New Guinea's
logo and metallic security thread.
   All the banknotes feature the Papua New Guinea national crest on
the front. Each note is distinguished by
the different background tints surrounding the crest which depict
various traditional motifs.

                                          Description of Currency-

Two Kina K2


     (a) Front:-The background tints surrounding the national crest
on the front of the note comprise a tapa

cloth from the Central District, a Mount Hagen axe, a club from the
Huon Gulf area, a clay pot from the Sepik,

a shield from the Madang area, a marriage bed from Manus Island and
a shield from the Upper Sepik region.


     The designs surrounding the numerals represent local lineal art
patterns in modern style and do not interpret

any particular subject.


     (b) Back:-The back of this banknote features four main items: a
Mount Hagen axe, a kula arm band from

the Milne Bay District, engraved dogs teeth from the Bougainville
area and a clay pot from the Sepik. The back-

ground tints comprise patterns taken from a tapa cloth from the

Northern District, waist bands from the Gulf

District, a canoe from the Trobriand Islands, a shield from the
Sepik area, a canoe from the West Sepik area, a

Madang shield and clubs from the Huon Gulf region.


     The patterns used to surround the numerals in local artwork are
based on a bird design.


Five Kina K5


     (a) Front:-The background tints surrounding the national crest
on the front of this banknote comprise pat-

terns taken from the following items: a shield from the Gulf
District, a Sepik clay pot and Ramu River shields

from the Madang area. The patterns surrounding the numerals are
based on a slaughtered pig design.


     (b) Back:-The main designs on the back of the banknote comprise
four items of traditional Papua New

Guinea ''currencies": a Hombuli mask which is used for bridal
payments in the Sepik area, a kina shell from the

Highlands, a shell necklace from the Milne Bay area and a shell
necklace woven with seeds found in the New

Ireland District. The background tints for this design consist of a
Northern District tapa cloth, a Milne Bay shield

and tortoise shell bracelets from the Huon Gulf area.


     The patterns used to surround the numerals are based on a mask
design together with an illustration of a

bird.


Ten Kina K10


     (a) Front:-The background tints surrounding the national crest
on the front of this banknote include patterns

taken from the following items: a canoe from the Milne Bay District,
Sepik spears, a Madang shield, designs based

on patterns seen on a bow from the Highlands, a Sepik house post and
wood carvings from the New Ireland area.

The patterns surrounding the numerals are based on an illustration
of a bird.


     (b) Back:-The main design on the back of this banknote is
composed of the following items: a Tami bowl,

a bird of paradise skin, tambu shell money from the New Britain area
and boars tusks from the Highlands.


     The pattern surrounding the numeral is based on a
representation of a bird and a fish.


     The background tints for this banknote include patterns taken
from a Gulf shield, a ceremonial dance paddle

from Bougainville, a Sepik clay pot, a Gulf bark belt and marriage
bed posts from the Manus District.

                               MAXIMUM PRICES FOR BREAD—WEWAK


  MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller appointed
under the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as


  amended to date, hereby make the following Order under that Act:—


                                             PRICES ORDER No. 136


1. CITATION.

    This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 136.

2. COMMENCEMENT.


    This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazelle.


3. REVOCATION.


    Prices Order No. 95 is hereby revoked.


4. DEFINITIONS.

    In this Order—


       "bread" means a product obtained by baking a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with or


            without other ingredients;


       "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or


            milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;


       "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per centum


            by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the
water-free substance;


       "starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread ' means
bread which is made into loaves and which con-


            tains not less than two and seven-tenths part per centum
by weight of nitrogen calculated on the water-

free substance;


       "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in this


            Order.


       "wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery to the


            place at which the bread is sold by retail, in waxed or
grease-proof paper, cellulose film, polythene or


            other similar wrapping and that such bread was so
enclosed when sold;


       "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread
that such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery


            to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was


            so enclosed when sold;


5. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.


    Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be measured


when the bread is cold.


6. MAXIMUM PRICE.


    I fix and declare the maximum price at which bread included in a
category described in the first column of

the Schedule to this Order may be sold by retail in the town of
Wewak to he the price specified in the second column

of that Schedule opposite to the description of that category.


7. DISPLAY OF PRICES.


    A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the Town of Wewak, shall display in each


of their places of business, in prominent positions and in large
clear and legible figures, the types of bread loaves


covered by this Order and the prices at which such loaves may be
bought.
